correctness.rationale: GKZ dimension and face-lattice theorem identify the polar boundary with the diagonal complex. Three exact affine constraints leave the full (n-3)-dimensional Fourier complement. Rotation-equivariant radial projection provides a sphere action. Prime weights are faithful and composite divisor weights give fixed vectors, and standard lens-space topology yields the stated groups and cup products. Finite verifier checked Catalan counts and fixed subspaces for specific cases; no finite test substitutes for the general proof.

value.rationale: The prime regular-polygon diagonal complex is a canonical sphere with a natural cyclic symmetry, so its geometric orbit-space homeomorphism type is motivated. Explicit Fourier weights determine exact lens-space types and yield arbitrarily many degrees of p-torsion, beyond existing finite-face cyclic-sieving counts. The sharp free-action boundary is geometric and uniform, not a routine table of small examples.
